explanation: Rhodes panel expressly overruled Copelin's sua sponte limiting-instruction rule, but the footnote states the overruling was circulated to and approved by the full court (Irons v. Diamond procedure), also resting on Fed. R. Evid. 105; limb 3 fails.

Buss expressly overruled Riley (and Slack) in a footnote, but it was decided by seven judges of the Commonwealth Court sitting en banc (President Judge Craig and six judges), not a three-judge panel; limb 2 fails.

Ionics panel overruled Roto-Lith, but footnote says departure was compelled by the statute itself and the opinion was circulated to all active judges, none of whom objected; recognised First Circuit informal en banc circulation, so limb 3 fails.

Ortiz panel overruled Collado's reading of 21 U.S.C. 851(a)(2), but footnote states the opinion was circulated before filing to all active judges with no objection (Second Circuit mini en banc); limb 3 fails.

De Jesus (3d DCA panel) receded from American Service Mutual v. Wilson, not the named Werner decision, a Fourth DCA per curiam sharing page 645; different case and district. It also relied on earlier Florida Supreme Court authority (Rutkin). Limb 1 fails.

Hobbs expressly overruled Collier v. Marsh and Jones v. Cropps in part, but eight judges participated (author plus seven concurring, one not participating), i.e. the whole nine-judge Georgia Court of Appeals as then constituted, not a three-judge division; limb 2 fails.

LaFountain panel overruled McGore's no-leave-to-amend rule, but expressly because McGore is flatly inconsistent with the intervening Supreme Court decision in Jones v. Bock (2007); recognised intervening higher-court ground, so limb 3 fails.
